nodes.title: Window chrome buttons are on the left in Electron 38.2.0 on Ubuntu 22
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 38.2.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version 22.04 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 38.1.2 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Window chrome buttons respect OS style and settings in Ubuntu Linux. (Like in Ubuntu 24 or older Electron releases, see bellow.) See the screenshot from Ubuntu 22 with the app based on Electron 37 ### Actual Behavior When we have upgraded our app to **Electron 38.2.0** and window chrome buttons moved to the left while other other **Ubuntu 22** apps (including GNOME apps) have the window chrome buttons on the right side. Furthermore, when I click by right mouse button on the window title bar, context menu appears, that's OK. But since then, the context menu appears for every mouse click does not matter which button. So, left mouse click to window chrome buttons opens context menu - **the buttons do not work since then**. I cannot even move the window with mouse. I have to restart the app. ### Testcase Gist URL The "Hello World!" app Fiddle creates on start ### Additional Information I have on my Ubuntu 22 GNOME settings: ``` $ gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-layout ':minimize,maximize,close' $ echo $XDG_SESSION_TYPE wayland ``` Further testing: * Ubuntu 22 and Electron 37 or lower: window chrome buttons work well (i.e. like other apps). * Ubuntu 24 and Electron 38.2.0: window chrome buttons work well (i.e. like other apps). * Ubuntu 22 and Google Chrome 140.0.7339.127: window chrome buttons have a bit different style, but are on the right side and work well. **Update:** * `unset XDG_SESSION_TYPE` fixed the problem on Ubuntu 22 with Electron 38.2.0.

nodes.title: Too much memory usage building v38.1.2 on Ubuntu 22
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 38.1.2 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 37.5.1 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior "e build electron" succeeds after a couple of hours ### Actual Behavior My 24GB of memory usage skyrockets and my 10GB swap file fills up, eventually crashing the build process. There are way too many activate node and clang++ processes running and apparently not being shut down as their job completes, maybe. Normally there are only a few node and clang++ processes at any given moment. And normally memory usage hangs out around 4-5 GB. To Reproduce: Follow instructions to build version v38.1.2 tag on an Ubuntu macthine. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Node version v22.13.1 I use this same linux box to build versions every couple of months, the last version I was able to build successfully was v37.3.1. I'm not sure if there is a change that caused this in the electron source, or build-tools, or if it's related to regular system updates to Ubuntu. Building electron v37.5.1 doesn't seem to have this problem. I wasn't sure if this issue should be opened in the electron project or the build-tools project, the dupe in build-tools is here https://github.com/electron/build-tools/issues/753 Feel free to cancel either issue.

38.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10.0.18362

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When I call console.log() from the main process, message written to stdout (command prompt on windows)

When I call console.log() from renderer process, message written to devTools ONLY

### Actual Behavior

When I call console.log() from the main process, message written to stdout (command prompt on windows)

When I call console.log() from renderer process, message written to devTools AND stdout

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This only occurs when using a persistent session. Non-persistent sessions behave as expected.

set ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING = false has no effect

I can find nothing in the official docs to explain why this happens or how to prevent it.

This is potentially a huge security issue, apart from making stdout unreadable. It seems ridiculous that this behaviour is the default for persistent sessions, and there is no way to change it...

nodes.title: Wayland app_id should be normalized to match wm_class
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 38 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Fedora 42 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Apps should have the same wm_class (X11) and app_id (Wayland) by default. This allows desktop environments to look up the correct icons on both X11 and Wayland, based on a single .desktop file. e.g.., an app with `productName: "1Password"` should have its wm_class and app_id both normalized to "1password" to correspond with a "1password.desktop" file. It might also be a good idea to let developers specify the app_id and/or wm_class at runtime instead of relying on hard-to-understand semantics from fields in package.json. ### Actual Behavior Electron sets a lowercase wm_class but preserves the case when setting app_id, deriving both values from the same fields in package.json (`productName` or `name`). If the source value isn't already lowercase, this causes some icons not loading properly on Wayland in certain environments, e.g. KDE. An example is 1Password, which shows its icon in the taskbar icon but is unable to show it in the Alt-Tab switcher or window corner when running in native Wayland mode: - productName: "1Password" - derived wm_class: `1password` - derived app_id: `1Password` - desktop file: `1password.desktop` ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information xdg documentation: https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_toplevel:request:set_app_id

nodes.title: [Feature Request] Support tag and renotify from the Web Notification API in new Notification() (Electron)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

### **Summary**
Add tag and renotify options to Electron.Notification so apps can replace/coalesce notifications (by tag) and optionally re-alert the user when a tagged notification is updated—matching the Web Notification API semantics. See Electron’s current Notification docs and tutorial.

### **Motivation & Use Cases**

- Chat/Collab apps: keep only the latest per-thread/DM toast instead of spamming users; bump attention on important updates (renotify: true).
- Status summaries: “5 → 8 unread” replaces the same card by tag without adding a second toast.
- Cross-platform parity with Web: devs expect Web Notification API behavior in Electron renderers/main.

Pain today:
- No built-in way to replace the same logical notification.
- Apps must do OS-specific workarounds → inconsistent UX & more code.


### Proposed Solution

### **Proposed API**
interface NotificationConstructorOptions {
  // existing fields…
  tag?: string;       // Identifier to replace an existing notification with the same tag
  renotify?: boolean; // If replacing, re-alert user (sound/attention) when supported
}

### **Behavior**
- If tag is set and a visible (or Action Center/Notification Center) notification with the same tag exists, the new one replaces it.
- If renotify === true, replacement should re-alert where supported. If not supported, still replace (no-op on alert).



### Alternatives Considered

- App-level maps with manual .close() + .show(): works but error-prone and diverges per OS.
- Full custom toastXml on Windows only: loses cross-platform parity and adds platform branches.

### Additional Information

### **References**
[renotify](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notification/renotify)
[tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notification/tag)
[timestamp](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notification/timestamp)

nodes.title: `webRequest.onHeadersReceived` does not lower case header names
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.0

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unsure, also broken in 37

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

As per https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-5.1-3, HTTP headers should be treated as case insensitive. The `IncomingMessage` API already handles this by automatically lower-casing any incoming headers.

### Actual Behavior

The `responseHeaders` object contains headers in whatever case the server sent them in.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/devinbinnie/097a327168fd8353a7ea632d2618f07d

### Additional Information

This makes it difficult to predictably modify or track incoming headers.

Note: I noticed Chromium has an API like this for its extensions. I'm not sure if Electron under the hood uses this API, but if it's broken there I can file a ticket with Chromium. Would just need confirmation.

nodes.title: Significant performance regression between Electron 34.5 and 37.2
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

36.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.7

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

34.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

I maintain a note-taking app called [Reflect](https://reflect.app/). After updating Electron and shipping a new release, we immediately received reports that the app had slowed to a crawl on Intel Macs.

The app technically still runs, but performance is severely degraded. We’ve since rolled back to version 34.5, which was stable on Intel Macs. This suggests a performance regression introduced between the two Electron versions, but only affecting Intel Macs—Apple Silicon machines are unaffected.

One more detail: the user I debugged this with was on an Intel Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.7. At this point, I don’t have enough data to say whether the slowdown is tied specifically to Intel hardware, the OS version, or some combination. I’ll gather more bug reports and update once I know more.

### Actual Behavior

Big performance regression, see above. 

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Expose `xdg_toplevel::state` information on Wayland
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

[xdg_toplevel::state](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_toplevel:enum:state) is an enum of different states a window/toplevel can be in exposed as an array in [xdg_toplevel::configure](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_toplevel:event:configure).



### Proposed Solution

Specifically, I'd like access to the `tiled_*` information. `suspended` and `constrained_*` are not too useful for UI code, and are newer in the spec, so I don't expect those to be exposed.

Expose this information along the lines of `{ tiled: { left: boolean, right: boolean, etc. } }` on the window object through a (possibly Wayland only) API.

### Alternatives Considered

I believe native plugins are a thing. I'd consider using one of those if it is infeasible to expose in Electron directly.

### Additional Information

The `tiled_*` information is most useful when rendering rounded corners. If say the left side is tiled (an example of when is if the window was dragged to the left side of the monitor) knowing this in the application can conditionally apply window rounding for the sides that are not tiled.

I apologize if this information is already exposed. I wouldn't be surprised if similar information is exposed on Windows or OSX, and thus it is exposed under a different name. I only know the Wayland terminology.

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

37.5.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

37.2.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

In a transparent window, calling `setResizable(true)` should not cause the title bar to appear

### Actual Behavior

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/872a7690-195b-468f-af8a-55ffff7fcee1)

This also further affects the behavior of frameless transparent windows:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17b9c66d-2d4e-4b47-b56f-d980e4840557)

In a frameless transparent window, when an abnormal background appears, a window shadow also appears

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/7fbea9d7a1318da594819e8c99338184

### Additional Information

I checked the supported versions and 37.2.5 was the last version that worked properly, after that all versions up to v38 had issues.
I checked the changelog for 37.2.6 and it seems to be caused by this: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/47386

Additionally, I noticed that even with the transparent window set alone, the title bar will appear on startup:

```js
  const mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({
    height: 260,
    width: 300,
    transparent: true,
  })
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/940ba9eb-f0b9-484a-b0c0-228f7f61986b)

### Electron Version

38.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro, 24H2, 26100.6584, Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.234.0

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Frameless BrowserWindow should have rounded corners on Windows 11

### Actual Behavior

If you create a frameless window on Windows 11, there are tiny points in all four corners that make the window a perfect rectangle in shape as if it is running on Windows 10. The points appear behind the shadow/mask for it appearing to try to have rounded corners.

If you use `app.disableHardwareAcceleration();` then it works as expected and does not show points in the corners.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/jediwade/f360467ebbaf4967e2d635ad31af89d9

### Additional Information

_No response_
